text:
The Canadiens beat New Jersey 3-2 on Wednesday, handing Connor Hellebuyck his first loss as a Devils starter, and The Hockey News' Mike Fink called them the most skilled team the Devils have faced. Jake Evans scored the winner, with Lane Hutson picking up another assist. Montreal is 13-5-4 with 30 points.

They're doing it shorthanded. Chris Kreider is out six to eight weeks (NHL.com), Josh Anderson is on injured reserve, and Zachary Bolduc's status is a worry after the Devils game. The noise has been loud too: Cole Caufield's criticism of the officiating drew a reply from an NHL referee (Markerzone), and Arber Xhekaj acknowledged some frustration in the room (Montreal Hockey Fanatics).

Our numbers are the cold shower. Montreal has 48.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and allows 3.48 per 60 minutes. The goaltending has allowed 11.47 fewer goals than those chances usually produce, and we count about 7.3 more points than the play has earned. Jacob Fowler has been better than his save rate looks, .921 against hard shots and 4.4 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

The good lines are real: Phillip Danault, Alexandre Texier and Bolduc have 61% of the expected goals, and Noah Dobson with Hutson takes 57%. Our playoff odds are 68%. The bank of points is valuable; the process needs to catch up before it runs out.
headline: Montreal keeps winning, and the bodies keep falling
